purpose: Ethambutol is used to treat tuberculosis (TB), a serious infection that mainly affects the lungs. It is almost always used together with other TB medicines to fight the infection more effectively. It can also be used for certain other mycobacterial infections.
how_it_works: Ethambutol works by blocking the tuberculosis bacteria from building their outer protective wall. Without that wall, the bacteria cannot survive or multiply. This helps your immune system and the other TB medicines wipe out the infection over time.
common_side_effects: The most important side effect to watch for is changes in your vision, such as blurry vision, trouble telling red from green, or loss of sharpness — tell your doctor right away if this happens. Other side effects can include nausea, stomach upset, headache, dizziness, joint pain, and a skin rash.
warnings: Vision problems are the most serious risk with this medicine, so your doctor will check your eyesight before and during treatment. Tell your doctor immediately if you notice ANY change in your vision. Use with caution if you have kidney problems, since the drug can build up in your body. It is generally not recommended for children under 13 years old because young children cannot reliably report vision changes. Let your doctor know if you have gout, as this medicine can raise uric acid levels.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is based on your body weight — typically 15 to 25 mg per kilogram of body weight, taken once daily by mouth. Your doctor will calculate the exact dose for you. It is best taken with food if it upsets your stomach. TB treatment usually lasts many months, so it is very important to take every dose and not stop early, even if you feel better.
